output.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree native to open woodland in South Africa and Madagascar. It has large pale-green leaves and clusters of white flowers with red and yellow stamens that move rapidly when touched.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s central-west limestone region. It has fleshy, scalloped leaves, white flowers and dense glandular hairs, and grows mainly in limestone rock crevices and walls.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A perennial climbing vine native to Mexico’s Atlantic and Pacific coastal plains. It has large heart-shaped leaves and showy, usually pink flowers that may bloom throughout the year. Its tubers and seeds are edible; Indigenous inhabitants of Baja California Sur historically toasted and ground the seeds or boiled them for fried cakes.
output.edibilityNote: Tubers and seeds are edible; Baja California Sur’s Indigenous inhabitants historically toasted and ground seeds or boiled them for fried cakes.

output.summary: A submerged aquatic perennial native to Europe, Asia and North Africa. Its finely divided leaves grow in whorls, while its small orange-red flowers rise above the water. Broken stem fragments help it spread, and it can form dense invasive mats.
A flowering plant native to southern Mexico, Central America, Colombia and Venezuela. It has long, lance-shaped leaves and yellow flowers marked with brown spots.
A flowering grass whose listed subspecies are native to mainland Portugal; subsp. pratense is introduced in the Azores.

A fleshy flowering perennial native to mainland Portugal, the Azores and Madeira. Its rounded leaves have a navel-like central depression and form rosettes, while pale pink-green, bell-shaped flowers appear from May.

A flowering herbaceous perennial found across temperate Europe, Asia and eastern and western North America. It bears feathery plumes of white or cream flowers, with male and female flowers on separate plants. In Italy, young shoots are briefly boiled and then cooked with eggs and cheese or added to a wild-green soup.
output.edibilityNote: In Italy, young shoots are briefly boiled, then cooked with eggs and cheese or included in a traditional wild-green soup.

output.summary: A fan palm endemic to Guadalupe Island, Mexico. Its native trees occupy a small grove on the island’s steep northern end, where the maritime climate and terrain produce a rare North American fog oasis.

An evergreen conifer native to California’s Central Coast and Mexico’s Guadalupe and Cedros islands. Its bright-green needles usually grow in clusters of three, although var. binata has pairs. Its cones may remain closed until forest-fire heat opens them and releases the seeds.
A perennial grass with no native origin stated, tall wheatgrass has broad leaves and yellow flowers. Its self-supporting stems can reach about five feet.

A flowering plant with no native origin stated, claspingleaf St. John’s wort occurs from Florida to New York and in Guatemala. It favors wet habitats and has yellow, five-petalled flowers, with upper leaves much larger than lower ones.

An aquatic plant native to warm-temperate South America, Brazilian waterweed has trailing stems that root at intervals and leaves arranged in whorls. It can spread across the water surface as a dense, light-blocking canopy and has separate male and female plants.

A tropical to subtropical perennial grass native to Mexico and South America, bahiagrass is remembered for its prominent V-shaped flower head. Its creeping stems root along the ground and form dense turf.

A deciduous vine native to western North America, California wild grape climbs other plants or trails across the ground on twisted woody stems. Its small, often sour purple grapes ripen in autumn and are edible, including for making wine or jelly.
output.edibilityNote: Small, often sour purple grapes are eaten and can be made into wine or jelly.

output.summary: A flowering plant native to temperate North Africa, Europe and parts of western Asia, annual wall-rocket is annual but sometimes perennial. It has a basal rosette of lobed leaves, usually yellow flowers and long fruit capsules, and often grows on disturbed ground.

A clumping perennial herb native to South America, especially Argentina, fragrant heliotrope has branching hairy stems and abundant, wavy-edged leaves. Its curved flower spikes carry tiny bright-purple blooms with tubular yellow throats.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, clasping-leaved jointed glasswort tolerates salty conditions. In a 2016–2019 mainland Portuguese assessment, it was confined to a tiny area between Faro and Olhão, with fewer than 2,500 mature plants estimated and was assessed as Critically Endangered.

A small evergreen tree native to and found only in the Azores, Azores laurel is a major part of the islands’ laurel and high-elevation juniper forests. It also occurs on lava flows, in coastal and mountain scrub, and in forested peat bogs.

A plant native to Asia, Russia, Ukraine and Romania, Syrian bean-caper has thin stems with sparse, fleshy, waxy leaflets. Its long taproot can produce new plants from fragments, and it forms colonies in dry, gravelly, salty or disturbed places.

An evergreen shrub native to the Atlantic coasts of western Europe. Its green, spiny stems largely take over the work of its reduced leaves, and yellow flowers appear mainly in late summer and autumn. It can regrow from its roots after fire, while slight scorching encourages seed germination.

A deciduous, often multi-stemmed shrub found across most of North America. Its nut sits inside a beak-like husk whose tiny filaments can irritate skin. Indigenous peoples ate and commonly traded the nuts, which have the same uses as other hazelnuts.
output.edibilityNote: The nuts were eaten and commonly traded among Indigenous groups and are used like other hazelnuts.

output.summary: A flowering plant native from the Caucasus through Central Asia to the western Himalaya. It tolerates poor soil, drought and nearby paving, making it suitable as a street tree.

An epiphyte or tree found from Mexico to Costa Rica and in the Antilles. It has cream-coloured latex and petals, while its rounded fruit remains green when mature. It grows in evergreen or secondary forests and along roadsides in the Atlantic zone.

A large, single-stemmed aloe of Southern Africa, ranging from the Johannesburg area through parts of Botswana, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Eswatini and Mozambique. It bears a robust crown of stiff grey-green leaves, usually with many short spines. Its winter flower clusters typically branch horizontally and range from yellow through orange to bright red.

An evergreen perennial native to the eastern and central United States. It forms low mats of hairy, narrow leaves, covered in late spring and early summer by small flowers in shades including pink, white, blue and mauve.
A small flowering plant native to Europe and parts of North Africa and the Middle East.

An aquatic plant found in slow or still waters from Central America to northern Canada, with additional reports from Brazil and Guyana. Its fragrant white flowers open by day, close at night and pull their developing fruit underwater after pollination. Its seeds, flowers and rhizomes can be eaten raw or cooked.
output.edibilityNote: The seeds, flowers and rhizomes are edible either raw or cooked.

output.summary: A strongly branched evergreen shrub native to the Himalayas, western China, India and Nepal. Its vivid gentian-blue flowers emerge from green-and-white veined bracts that remain after flowering, and its large dark-green leaves are hairy.
A flowering plant whose varieties frutescens and latifolia are documented as native to mainland Portugal.

An aquatic perennial native to Eurasia and the Americas, longleaf pondweed grows in ponds, lakes, ditches and streams. Its submerged leaves are narrow while its floating leaves are oval, and both types are carried on notably long stalks.

An evergreen fern native to the Americas, the southern sword fern has long, highly divided fronds and a slim, tuberous underground stem. Wild plants have erect fronds, while the Boston fern and some other cultivars arch gracefully.

A coniferous tree native to eastern Canada and the north-central and northeastern United States, northern white-cedar has fan-like branches, flat sprays of scale-like leaves and peeling red-brown bark. Some cliff-growing specimens are exceptionally old but remain small and stunted.
output.edibilityNote: Ojibwa reportedly made soup from soft-twig inner bark; twigs were also brewed as tea. Prolonged internal use or use during pregnancy may be harmful.

output.summary: A conspicuous moss found chiefly in the north Atlantic, golden-head moss has strongholds in western Britain, Ireland and western Norway. It occurs most often in upland acidic grassland, especially near wet flushes.
A flowering plant endemic to coastal Portugal, Herniaria maritima inhabits clearings among creeping woodland and junipers on fixed coastal dunes. It grows on sandy soils that are neutral or alkaline.
A flowering plant native to Asia, threelobe spirea has occasionally become naturalized in the United States.
A flowering plant native to the western and central Mediterranean, Asparagus albus occurs in coastal shrubland and disturbed places.

A deciduous small tree or large shrub native to Europe and northern and northeastern Asia, bird cherry bears drooping clusters of flowers and black, strongly astringent fruit. In Russia, dried berries are milled into flour for cakes, while fresh fruit may be minced and cooked as jam; some parts, including the fruit, contain potentially poisonous glycosides.
output.edibilityNote: In Russia, dried berries are milled into flour for cake; fresh fruit may be minced and cooked as jam. Fruit can contain potentially poisonous glycosides.

output.summary: A lycophyte native to Mexico and Central America, Selaginella martensii is commonly known as variegated spikemoss or Martens's spike moss.

A perennial subshrub or small shrub native to Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, northern South America and southern Florida. Its bright yellow flowers open around sunrise and close or wilt by midday, while its mature capsules split to release seeds.

An annual, occasionally biennial herb native to the western Mediterranean, Albania and Macaronesia. Its solitary flower heads generally hang before flowering, and its brown fruits occur in two markedly different forms.
An annual herb native to northern North America. Its heads contain orange florets and usually lack yellow rays; its flat dark fruits bear two hornlike, barbed tips that catch on animals.

A leafy liverwort with no native origin specified, distributed across Europe, Macaronesia, Japan and North America. It forms dense green-to-brown carpets, sometimes reddish in sunny places, and produces dark-brown oval spore capsules that mature in spring.

A low-growing evergreen shrub native to China, Afghanistan, northeastern India, Bhutan and Nepal. It bears fragrant white flowers throughout winter, followed by black berries; its varieties can differ greatly in appearance.

A pear species native to central and eastern Europe and western Asia. Most orchard pears grown in Europe, North America and Australia derive from it; the fruit is eaten fresh or cooked and fermented into perry.
output.edibilityNote: Pears are eaten fresh or cooked in desserts and pies, served with meat, or fermented into perry and distilled into pear brandy.

output.summary: A small annual herb with no native origin stated. It has a self-supporting form and broad, compound leaves.

A marine red alga native to China, Japan, Korea and parts of eastern Russia. Its soft, gelatinous blades range from red to burgundy, becoming yellow when dying or dead, and several blades may arise from one central attachment. It is edible.
output.edibilityNote: The seaweed is stated to be edible, without details about parts or preparation.

output.summary: A tuberous perennial herb native around the Black Sea and in a separate Mediterranean population from Turkey’s Hatay Province through Lebanon to northern Israel. Its rounded or heart-shaped leaves vary from green to silver-patterned, and its squat pink, magenta or white flowers bloom from winter into spring.

A perennial herb native to Europe, Asia, Africa and North America. It spreads by rooting runners and bears tight spikes of purple, sometimes white, two-lipped flowers. Young leaves and stems are eaten raw, the whole plant boiled as a vegetable, and above-ground parts brewed cold as a drink.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves and stems are eaten raw; the whole plant is boiled as a vegetable, and aerial parts make a cold-infused beverage.

output.summary: A deciduous perennial fern native to Eurasia and North America. Large triangular fronds rise singly from underground rhizomes, forming dense, exceptionally long-lived colonies, while coiled silver-grey shoots emerge in spring.
output.edibilityNote: Young shoots, fronds, starch and rhizomes have been eaten; traditional preparation includes soaking and cooking, but authorities warn against consumption because of toxicity.

output.summary: A fibre crop native from Mexico to Ecuador and northeastern Brazil, parts of the Caribbean, and several Pacific islands. Its cultivars account for about 90% of global cotton production, and its varieties differ notably in fibre length.

A bushy perennial flowering shrub native to parts of the Mediterranean and Middle East. Its golden-yellow flowers have conspicuously long stamens, and its leaves usually produce a goat-like smell, though one subspecies lacks it.
A perennial grass native across much of Europe, Asia and Africa. It commonly grows beneath forest canopies and has drooping leaves and narrow, drooping flower spikes.

A large oak tree native to eastern and central North America. It can withstand seasonal flooding, and its bristle-tipped, lobed leaves develop relatively late brown-to-red autumn colour that varies by region.

A medium-sized red marine alga whose native origin is not specified; it occurs from Norway and the Faroes to Senegal, the Mediterranean and the Canary Islands. Its flattened branches alternate between long and short forms, with curved side branches creating a comb-like pattern.

An annual or biennial mustard-family herb native to much of North America and Central America. Its branched flower clusters resemble bottlebrushes, bearing small white flowers followed by greenish fruits. Young leaves are eaten raw or cooked, while young seedpods serve as a black-pepper substitute.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves are eaten raw, sautéed or as a cooked green; young seedpods are used as a black-pepper substitute.

output.summary: A summer annual flowering plant native to Eurasia. Its numerous wiry, zigzagging stems spread into a mat, and it thrives in compacted soil and survives drought.
A plant species native to the Madeira archipelago. It has a zigzagging taproot with whitish, soft, brittle and juicy roots.

A scrambling perennial plant native from Mexico and the Caribbean through Central and South America to Argentina and Bolivia. It may creep over the ground or climb trees as a woody vine, bearing yellow flower heads and narrow fruits tipped with two backward-barbed points.
A flowering plant native to a range extending from Europe to China.

An erect, deciduous shrub found in central and southern Europe, particularly in woods, scrub and rocky slopes. Its many smooth, thorny branches carry clustered leaves, and it produces greenish fruits with two or three stones.
An aquatic plant widespread across Europe and Asia and naturalized in many other regions. It generally grows in wet places at lower elevations.

A medium-sized tree fern native to New Zealand. It is slow-growing and long-lived, with a thick, soft, rusty-brown fibrous trunk and a distinctive skirt of retained dead leaves. A local Tauranga variety regularly branches into numerous forks.

A biennial thistle native to southwestern Europe. Its tall, branching stem and deeply lobed leaves are spiny, while its large flower heads contain many narrow purple flowers and have woolly or cobweb-like coverings.

A bushy evergreen perennial native to southern Europe and southwestern Asia. It has somewhat fleshy leaves arranged in spirals and bears clusters of bright yellow flowers in late spring. Broken parts release a milky sap that can irritate skin.
output.edibilityNote: All parts are toxic if eaten.

output.summary: A flowering shrub native to the Indian subcontinent, Tibet, Sichuan and Yunnan in China, and Myanmar. It is low, spreading and rabbit-tolerant, making it suitable for rock gardens and hedges, though it can become invasive.
An evergreen tree native to South Africa.
A flowering plant in the pea family, introduced in both mainland Portugal and Madeira.

An annual grass native to the Old World, it now occurs worldwide as an introduced species and sometimes a noxious weed. Its dense, greenish flower head looks soft and feathery because the spikelets bear long, fine, whitish bristles.
A flowering plant in the sedge family native to mainland Portugal.

A perennial wetland plant native across most of Eurasia and North America, and more locally in Africa and South America. Its adjoining male and female flower sections develop into the familiar brown, sausage-shaped seed head, which persists through winter before breaking apart in spring.
output.edibilityNote: Rhizomes require cooking and skinning; peeled stems and leaf bases may be raw or cooked. Young spikes, shoots and sprouts are edible; avoid polluted or bitter specimens.

output.summary: A small, delicate fern occurring across the Mediterranean basin, it depends on seasonal flooding in temporary freshwater pools. Its spores survive the dry period but germinate only when the ground is completely saturated.

A creeping perennial native across Europe, Asia and Africa. Its trailing stems root at their joints, while long stalks carry solitary yellow flowers with five heart-shaped petals, blooming from June to September in Europe.

A rock-dwelling plant found in South Africa’s summer-rainfall areas, though not endemic there. Each leaf-pair flowers and is replaced by a new pair as the old one shrivels; collection for medicinal markets has contributed to declining numbers.

A deciduous vine native to the Caribbean and Central America, it bears exceptionally large flowers smelling of rotting meat. The heart-shaped, purple-veined flowers have long tails and attract flies, while the plant contains carcinogenic aristolochic acid.

An aquatic flowering plant native to the Azores. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment found its historical distribution uncertain because of repeated confusion with a similar species; it was then known only from Algarve and Baixo Alentejo and assessed as Vulnerable.

A small cactus native to Nuevo León and Coahuila, Mexico, where it grows in desert and dry scrub. Its rounded, densely spined stems produce tiny pink daytime flowers followed in summer by slender, bright-red fruits that quickly become papery.

An upright shrub endemic to central eastern New South Wales, especially associated with sandstone country around Sydney. It has thin, firm bark, broad pointed leaves, relatively large white or pink flowers, and mature fruit that remains on the plant.
A shrub or tree endemic to the Canary Islands. It is conservation-dependent.
A slender tree endemic to eastern Australia. Its drooping branchlets bear leaves reduced to tiny scales, while its warty, barrel-shaped cones contain brown winged seeds.
A green alga with a generally worldwide distribution across Atlantic and Pacific waters. Its branched fronds are completely tubular with rounded tips, and it may reproduce throughout the year.

A substantial evergreen shrub endemic to Taiwan, where habitat loss threatens it. It has large, hand-shaped leaves and produces spherical clusters of cream or white winter flowers followed by black fruit in spring.

A tropical tree native to the Greater Sunda Islands, Malay Peninsula, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Its crushed leaves are aromatic, and its edible bell-shaped berries have thin skin and white, spongy flesh; they are eaten fresh and used in salads, sautéed dishes, and pickles.
output.edibilityNote: The edible fruit is eaten fresh, in salads and lightly sautéed dishes, and made into pickles in Indian Ocean island cuisines.

output.summary: A small, variable succulent native to South Africa’s Western Cape Province. It usually has sharp triangular leaves with channels, keels and faint striped bands of spots, and it can form dense clumps.

An upright flowering tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It grows in shady forests and thickets and has slightly inrolled leaves, elongated pyramidal flower clusters and white bell-shaped flowers.
A flowering plant whose variety sabularia is endemic to mainland Portugal. That variety is protected under Portuguese or European legislation.

A red alga distributed across the Atlantic and Mediterranean. Its pink to dark-red body attaches to rock or other algae by creeping cylindrical filaments and develops flattened, irregularly branched upright axes; it commonly occupies dim, shallow rocky habitats year-round.
A multicellular marine red alga found in Europe, Africa, Brazil, Australia and some Atlantic islands.
A stonewort with a cosmopolitan distribution.
